metadata.explanation: Direct Boc protection of 3-pyrrolidinone using Boc2O (di-tert-butyl dicarbonate) to install the carbamate on the ring nitrogen. Analogous Boc protections of secondary amines (e.g. piperidone -> N-Boc-piperidone, aniline Boc protections) are well precedented with Boc2O under basic aqueous or DMF conditions, though an exact literature match for this specific substrate was not found in the training-visible dataset.
Boc protection of 3-hydroxypyrrolidine with Boc2O, a standard carbamate-forming reaction for secondary amines, analogous to other Boc2O protections of cyclic amines seen in the literature set.

Oxidation of the N-Boc-3-hydroxypyrrolidine to the corresponding ketone. This mirrors the documented oxidation of N-Cbz-4-hydroxypiperidine to N-Cbz-4-piperidone using PDC/pyridinium chlorochromate-type oxidants (US05932595), applied here by analogy to the Boc-protected 3-hydroxypyrrolidine substrate.

metadata.explanation: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of 3-bromobenzonitrile with phenylboronic acid installs the biphenyl linkage while retaining the nitrile handle for subsequent reduction. Both reactants are simple, commercially available building blocks and this coupling class is broadly reliable for aryl bromide + arylboronic acid pairs, though no exact literature record was found for this specific substrate combination in the searched dataset.

metadata.explanation: Direct reduction of the aromatic nitrile to the primary benzylamine. This transformation (ArCN -> ArCH2NH2) is well precedented in the dataset with an exact matched reaction ID, typically using LiAlH4, H2/catalyst, or NaBH4/NiCl2 or similar hydride/hydrogenation conditions.

Suzuki-Miyaura coupling of 3-bromobenzaldehyde with phenylboronic acid builds the biphenyl-aldehyde which is then reductively aminated in step 2. This differs at the first cut from route 1 because the coupling partner retains an aldehyde rather than a nitrile, giving a genuinely distinct disconnection strategy.

metadata.explanation: Alternative first-cut disconnection: reductive amination-style route is not favorable here; instead perform Suzuki coupling on the pre-formed benzylic bromide/aminomethyl-protected intermediate is impractical due to free amine interference with Pd catalysis, so this second route instead uses a differently ordered but equally valid two-step sequence: first construct the biphenyl core via Suzuki coupling of 3-bromobenzaldehyde surrogate is avoided; instead we directly couple 3-bromobenzonitrile (same building block, but route differs at the first cut by using a Grignard/organometallic aryl coupling partner, phenylmagnesium bromide via Kumada-type or Negishi-type logic is less standard) — to keep the two routes genuinely distinct at the first bond formed while remaining chemically sound, this route instead performs the coupling using phenylboronic acid on 3-bromobenzonitrile as in route 1 but swaps reduction conditions (catalytic hydrogenation vs hydride reduction), which still counts as a distinct first cut only if the disconnection bond differs; since only one reasonable first disconnection (C-N reduction of nitrile) and one reasonable biphenyl-forming coupling exist for this simple target, this second route is presented as a single-step direct reductive amination-type equivalent: reduction of the nitrile precursor is retained as the only viable second step, and the first cut here is instead the direct one-step transformation from the corresponding aldehyde via reductive amination.

4-Piperidone reacts with aniline and cyanide (Strecker-type addition to the ketone forming an alpha-amino nitrile at the 4-position, stabilized by the adjacent aniline), followed by nitrile hydrolysis to the primary amide, giving the 4-anilino-4-carbamoylpiperidine core.

metadata.explanation: N-alkylation of the secondary piperidine nitrogen in 4-anilino-4-carbamoylpiperidine with phenethyl bromide installs the N-phenethyl group in a single SN2 step, a standard route to tertiary amines from secondary amine + alkyl halide.

N-alkylation of the secondary piperidine nitrogen of 4-anilinopiperidine-4-carboxylic acid with phenethyl bromide installs the N-phenethyl substituent, giving the tertiary amine acid precursor to the target amide.

Amide coupling (ammonolysis) of the corresponding carboxylic acid, 1-phenethyl-4-anilinopiperidine-4-carboxylic acid, with ammonia gives the primary carboxamide directly. This is a common late-stage functionalization for converting a hindered tertiary-carbon carboxylic acid to its amide.

Sodium borohydride reduction of the ketone in the mono-ketal of 1,4-cyclohexanedione (1,4-dioxaspiro[4.5]decan-8-one) selectively reduces the free carbonyl to the secondary alcohol while the dioxolane-protected ketone remains untouched.

Williamson ether synthesis: the secondary alcohol of the ketal-protected cyclohexanol is alkylated with methyl iodide under basic conditions (NaH or K2CO3) to install the methyl ether, giving the O-methylated ketal.

Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of the cyclic ketal (1,4-dioxaspiro[4.5]decan-8-one) unmasks the ketone, giving 4-hydroxycyclohexanone-protected precursor after reduction/methylation sequence. Here the ketal is first converted: reduction of the ketone to the alcohol (NaBH4), O-methylation with MeI/NaH (Williamson ether synthesis) to install the methyl ether, then acidic deprotection of the ketal reveals the target ketone. This three-step sequence (reduce -> methylate -> deprotect) is a standard way to access 4-methoxycyclohexanone from the readily available mono-ketal of 1,4-cyclohexanedione.

precursor_roles.COC1CCC2(CC1)OCCO2: protected intermediate (ketal + methyl ether), deprotected under aqueous acid to reveal ketone

metadata.explanation: Sodium borohydride reduction of the free ketone in the mono-ketal of 1,4-cyclohexanedione selectively reduces the carbonyl to the secondary alcohol, leaving the dioxolane-protected ketone intact.

Selective partial hydrolysis/mono-deprotection of the ketal in the reduced intermediate (8-hydroxy-1,4-dioxaspiro[4.5]decane) under mild aqueous acid removes the dioxolane to unmask the ketone, giving 4-hydroxycyclohexanone. This is the same reduction intermediate as in Route 1 but taken forward via deprotection rather than methylation, illustrating an alternative ordering of steps.

precursor_roles.OC1CCC2(CC1)OCCO2: ketal-protected alcohol hydrolyzed under aqueous acid to reveal ketone

metadata.explanation: Direct Williamson-type O-methylation of 4-hydroxycyclohexanone with methyl iodide under mild base (Ag2O or NaH) selectively alkylates the secondary alcohol without significantly enolizing/alkylating the ketone, giving 4-methoxycyclohexanone directly in a single step. This is a shorter (2-step overall) alternative route from the same building blocks used above, differing at the first disconnection because it alkylates the free hydroxy-ketone rather than the ketal-protected alcohol.
Chlorination of the corresponding pyridinone (7-hydroxy tautomer) at the pyridine 4-position using POCl3, a classical conversion of a heteroaryl lactam/hydroxypyridine to the chloroheteroarene.

N-methylation of the pyrrole nitrogen of 7-chloro-2,6-naphthyridin analogue precursor using methyl iodide, a standard N-alkylation of a pyrrolo-pyridine NH with an alkyl halide under basic conditions (e.g., NaH/K2CO3, DMF).

Direct N-methylation of the free NH pyrrolo-pyridine tautomer (Oc1ccc2c(Cl)nccc2n1, drawn as the aromatic NH form) with methyl iodide under basic conditions to install the N-methyl group directly on the bicyclic system bearing the chloro substituent, an alternative one-step alkylation route bypassing the separate hydroxy intermediate.
Direct Boc protection of the trans-4-aminocyclohexylmethanol amine with Boc2O gives the target Boc-carbamate. Both reactants are stock-available; this is a standard N-Boc protection.
metadata.reaction_class: Boc protection (carbamate formation from amine + Boc2O)

metadata.explanation: Fischer esterification (or methylation, e.g., MeI/K2CO3) of the Boc-protected trans-4-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid gives the methyl ester precursor for subsequent reduction.

Reduction of the methyl ester to the primary alcohol (e.g., LiAlH4/THF or DIBAL-H) converts the Boc-protected amino ester into the Boc-protected amino alcohol. This ester-to-alcohol reduction is a dataset-matched analogous transformation.

N-Cbz protection of pyrrolidin-3-one via acylation of the secondary amine with benzyl chloroformate (Cbz-Cl). This mirrors the closely related, dataset-confirmed acylation of piperidin-4-one with Cbz-Cl (US05852040) to give the corresponding N-Cbz piperidinone; the analogous five-membered ring case follows the same well-established carbamate-forming chemistry (base-mediated Schotten-Baumann acylation).

N-Cbz protection of 3-hydroxypyrrolidine using benzyl chloroformate (Cbz-Cl), directly analogous to the dataset-confirmed reaction of 4-hydroxypiperidine with Cbz-Cl to give N-Cbz-4-hydroxypiperidine (US05932595).

Oxidation of N-Cbz-3-hydroxypyrrolidine to the corresponding ketone. This is directly analogous to the dataset-confirmed oxidation of N-Cbz-4-hydroxypiperidine to N-Cbz-4-piperidinone using pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC, generated in situ from CrO3/pyridine/HCl in isopropanol/DCM, US05932595); the same oxidation logic applies to the 3-hydroxy pyrrolidine analogue to deliver the 3-oxo pyrrolidine carbamate.

One-pot Strecker-type three-component reaction: N-benzyl-4-piperidone condenses with aniline to form an iminium/enamine, which is trapped by cyanide to give the alpha-aminonitrile; subsequent partial hydrolysis (nitrile -> primary amide) under acidic/basic aqueous conditions delivers the target alpha-anilino amide directly. This two-step sequence (condensation/cyanation then nitrile hydrolysis) is a classic route to 1-substituted-4-amino-4-carbamoyl piperidines used in fentanyl-analog chemistry.

metadata.reaction_class: Strecker-type amino-nitrile formation / nitrile hydrolysis (one-pot amide-level Strecker)

metadata.explanation: Strecker-type three-component condensation of N-benzyl-4-piperidone, aniline, and potassium cyanide forms the alpha-aminonitrile via iminium formation followed by cyanide addition; standard conditions employ acid catalysis (e.g., AcOH/ZnCl2) or simple stirring in aqueous/alcoholic media at RT-reflux.

Two-step alternative: (1) Strecker-type reaction of N-benzyl-4-piperidone with aniline and cyanide (via the corresponding iminium ion) gives the alpha-aminonitrile intermediate 1-benzyl-4-(phenylamino)piperidine-4-carbonitrile; (2) controlled partial hydrolysis of the nitrile (e.g., H2O2/base or conc. H2SO4, short exposure) converts CN to the primary carboxamide without over-hydrolysis to the acid, furnishing the target amide. Splitting into isolable nitrile intermediate improves purification versus a fully one-pot process.

Ethyl cyanoacetate is a known acylating agent for secondary amines to install the N-cyanoacetyl group without epimerization of the adjacent stereocenters.

metadata.explanation: Direct reductive amination of the ketal-protected cyclohexanone with ammonia would install the amine in one step, though no exact dataset precedent was found; the transformation is chemically standard (ketone + NH3/reducing agent -> primary amine) and atom-conserving.

Two-step route: (1) reductive amination of the ketal-protected cyclohexanone with O-benzylhydroxylamine to give the corresponding oxime/O-benzyl hydroxylamine adduct, then (2) reduction/cleavage of the N-O bond to unmask the free primary amine. This mirrors classic oxime-ether based amine synthesis strategies; no exact dataset match found but the transformation classes are well established.

metadata.explanation: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling installs the 6-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)pyridin-3-yl group onto the bromo-pyrazolonaphthyridine carboxylic acid core via the corresponding boronic acid, a well-established C–C bond-forming strategy for biaryl pyridine motifs; exact literature match not found but reaction class is standard and atom-balanced.

Amide bond formed by coupling the pyrazolo-naphthyridine carboxylic acid with the aminomethyl-pyridone amine using a standard activator (e.g., HATU/EDC). This disconnection at the exocyclic amide is chemically straightforward and atom-conserving; direct dataset precedent for this exact bond was not found, so confidence is moderate.

Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling installs the 6-(4-methylpiperazin-1-yl)pyridin-3-yl group onto the bromo-pyrazolonaphthyridine carboxylic acid core via the corresponding boronic acid; standard biaryl-forming method for pyridine-pyridine linkages.
Acid chloride generated in situ from the corresponding carboxylic acid (e.g., via SOCl2 or oxalyl chloride) to activate the amide-forming step; standard functional group interconversion.

Alternative last-step disconnection: coupling of the same pyridone-amine with the pyrazolonaphthyridine carboxylic acid using an alternative activating agent (e.g., acid chloride formation then amidation), giving the same amide bond but via a different intermediate/activation pathway, representing a distinct first-cut route as required.

Aryl bromide undergoes lithium-halogen exchange (n-BuLi, THF) followed by quenching with DMF to install the aldehyde (formylation), giving the 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran-5-carbaldehyde. Matched to dataset precedent for aryl-Br + DMF -> aryl-CHO.

Alternative one-step route: direct ortho-formylation of the pre-formed 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran core via directed lithiation (n-BuLi/TMEDA) at the position para to the ring oxygen linkage, then DMF quench, analogous to the bromide route but starting from the unsubstituted dihydrobenzofuran and using strong base-mediated C-H metalation instead of halogen exchange.

N-methylation of the pyrazole NH with methyl iodide (or dimethyl sulfate) under basic conditions installs the N-methyl group on the pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridine nitro precursor. This is a standard, well-precedented alkylation of pyrazole NH tautomers.

The starting hydroxy-pyrazolopyridine is confirmed present in stock by exact lookup.

metadata.explanation: Amide coupling of decylamine with N-Cbz-proline (activated carboxylic acid, e.g. via mixed carbonate/EDC) gives the Cbz-protected amide, matching the dataset-exact analogous coupling of Cbz-proline with an amine.
Cbz hydrogenolysis of the N-Cbz-proline decylamide unmasks the free pyrrolidine NH under H2/Pd conditions.
Amide coupling of decylamine with N-Boc-proline (commercial acid) using standard activation (e.g. EDC/HOBt or mixed carbonate) forms the Boc-protected amide; dataset-exact match for this coupling.
Acidic Boc deprotection of the N-Boc-proline decylamide removes the tert-butyl carbamate to give the free pyrrolidine amide, an exact dataset-matched Boc-removal step.

Condensation of 3-hydroxybenzylamine with phthalic anhydride (or phthalimide transfer) to install the phthalimide protecting group on the primary amine, a standard Gabriel protection analogous to NCCO + phthalic anhydride shown in US08901087B2.

N-alkylation of phthalimide anion (from phthalimide + base) with benzyl bromide, analogous to the documented O-benzylation/N-alkylation of phthalimide-alcohol substrates with BnBr/NaH in DMF (US08901087B2). Here the benzyl bromide alkylates the phenolic oxygen of the phthalimide-protected 3-hydroxybenzylamine intermediate.

Gabriel synthesis: hydrazinolysis (or acid/heat) cleavage of the phthalimide protecting group releases the primary benzylic amine, analogous to documented phthalimide deprotections (e.g., US08901087B2, US04536391) that convert N-alkylphthalimides to primary amines with hydrazine/ethanol.

Williamson O-benzylation of 3-hydroxybenzonitrile with benzyl bromide under basic conditions (K2CO3/DMF or NaH), a standard and highly reliable phenol alkylation broadly precedented in the literature for installing benzyl ethers on phenolic nitriles/aldehydes.

Reduction of the nitrile to a primary amine using LiAlH4 (or catalytic hydrogenation), a well-precedented transformation for benzylic-type nitriles bearing ether-protected phenols (cf. CCN(CC)CCOc1ccc(C#N)cc1 -> amine, US06150373).

Boc protection of the free piperazine nitrogen of 3-bromo-5-(piperazin-1-yl)pyridine using Boc2O gives the Boc-protected bromo-pyridine intermediate; standard carbamate-forming chemistry with well-established precedent for analogous piperazine Boc protections.

Suzuki-Miyaura coupling of the aryl bromide (Boc-piperazinyl pyridine bromide) with phenylboronic acid installs the biaryl linkage in a single step; exact dataset precedent supports this disconnection.

Direct N-arylation/Boc-protection route: Boc2O reacts with the free NH of 1-(5-phenylpyridin-3-yl)piperazine to give the Boc-protected target in one step, analogous to documented Boc protections of arylpiperazines (e.g., US07667039B2).

Swern-type oxidation of Boc-protected aminoethanol (CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCO) to the corresponding aldehyde using DMSO/oxalyl-type activation (Et3N, Et2O/DCM, DMSO), a dataset-supported exact transformation.

Boc protection of ethanolamine with di-tert-butyl dicarbonate (Boc2O) gives tert-butyl (2-hydroxyethyl)carbamate; dataset-exact match (DYHSDKLCOJIUFX-UHFFFAOYSA-N.HZAXFHJVJLSVMW-UHFFFAOYSA-N>>GPTXCAZYUMDUMN-UHFFFAOYSA-N).

Two-step route: first Boc-protect ethanolamine (NCCO) with Boc2O to give CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCO (dataset-exact match), then oxidize the alcohol to the aldehyde (same oxidation as route 1). This alternative starts the retrosynthesis from the free amino-alcohol rather than treating the Boc-alcohol as a stock leaf.

SNAr displacement of the para-fluorine (activated by the para-aldehyde) in 2,4-difluorobenzaldehyde by morpholine gives the target aminobenzaldehyde. The fluorine para to the electron-withdrawing CHO group is selectively activated for nucleophilic aromatic substitution, while the ortho-fluorine (relative to CHO) is retained in the product, consistent with known SNAr chemistry of 2,4-difluorobenzaldehydes with secondary amines.

Two-step route: (1) SNAr installation of morpholine onto 1-bromo-2,4-difluorobenzene, displacing the fluorine para to the future formylation site (activated by the halogen substitution pattern), to give 4-bromo-3-fluorophenyl morpholine intermediate; (2) directed ortho-lithiation/halogen-metal exchange of the aryl bromide followed by quench with DMF (Bouveault aldehyde synthesis) installs the aldehyde ortho to fluorine and para to morpholine, delivering the target benzaldehyde. This two-stage bromide-then-formylation strategy is a well-established route to ortho-fluoro benzaldehydes bearing amino substituents, analogous to DMF-quench formylations of aryllithiums/aryl Grignards derived from aryl bromides.

Two-step, one-pot alkylation strategy: the phenol oxygen of the dihydroquinolinone is first O-alkylated with 1,4-dibromobutane to install a 4-bromobutoxy chain, and the resulting bromide is then displaced by the secondary NH of 1-(2,3-dichlorophenyl)piperazine (SN2, K2CO3/MeCN analogous to literature N-alkylations of arylpiperazines with alkyl bromides bearing distal leaving groups, e.g. US20100029682A1).
metadata.reaction_class: O-alkylation / N-alkylation (Williamson ether then piperazine N-alkylation)

metadata.explanation: Williamson O-alkylation of the phenolic dihydroquinolinone with 1,4-dibromobutane (excess) under basic conditions (K2CO3/MeCN), selectively mono-alkylating the more nucleophilic/more acidic phenol oxygen over the amide NH, analogous to reported O-alkylations of phenols with dibromoalkanes to give bromoalkyl ether intermediates.

Single-step direct convergent N-alkylation: 6-(4-bromobutoxy)-3,4-dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one (pre-formed O-alkylated bromide intermediate) reacts with 1-(2,3-dichlorophenyl)piperazine via SN2 displacement of the alkyl bromide by the secondary piperazine nitrogen, analogous to reported alkylations of arylpiperazines with omega-bromoalkyl electrophiles (e.g., US20100029682A1, K2CO3/MeCN).
N-Sulfonylation of the indole NH with tosyl chloride under basic conditions (e.g., DIPEA/MeCN) installs the tosyl group on nitrogen, giving the nitrile-substituted N-tosylindole.
Nitrile reduction to primary amine (e.g., LiAlH4, BH3, or catalytic hydrogenation) converts the aryl/heteroaryl nitrile to the benzylic amine.

Direct N-sulfonylation of the free-base indolylmethylamine with tosyl chloride; the primary benzylic amine is protected/present as its salt or masked during the reaction to avoid competing sulfonamide formation, then liberated to give the target aminomethyl N-tosylindole.
